thesis: If an asset's positive daily bars achieve more range-normalized displacement per unit of relative activity than its negative bars, local demand is directionally asymmetric; persistent positive asymmetry with positive residual trend should identify continuation leaders.
primitive: Quantiacs daily OHLCV and historical is_liquid only
signal_contract: For each eligible asset/day, compute bounded displacement efficiency = abs(close-open log return) divided by same-day high-low range fraction, then discount it by positive log dollar-volume-share surprise using 1/(1+surprise). Over the rolling window compute the mean efficiency separately on positive and negative close-to-open bars with minimum observations. Base node is positive(upside-efficiency minus downside-efficiency), gated by positive 21-day residual trend.
ablation: use positive-bar efficiency level alone, removing the negative-bar comparison while keeping the same residual-trend gate
falsifier: deterministically rotate directional-asymmetry values across currently eligible identities before applying the same residual-trend gate
selection: positive scores, top five, deterministic label tie breaks
allocation: fixed slots min(0.25, 1/K); unused slots cash
cost_hypothesis: Directional asymmetry is slow-moving and weekly; fixed slots and immediate liquidity exits should remain compatible with the frozen cost ladder.
failure_mode: positive/negative bar comparison adds no information beyond positive-bar efficiency, or identity rotation preserves the result
stop_rule: freeze if matched ablation or destructive falsifier matches/beats the central parent, or if every valid base cell is below the fixed 1.0 development floor; do not invert, retune, or grid-rescue after observing failure
validation: 2023-2024 is SPENT_DO_NOT_MUTATE and excluded; 2025+ diagnostic and live evidence never drive mutation
contamination_notes: A-M volatility evidence is already observed. frontier_20260913m reserve returns were not observed before this preregistration. No Frontier-N returns were observed before freeze.
